problem:
Solve the inequality ${x}^{2}>12x$ and express the solution set in interval notation.

$x\in (${{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$)\,⋃\,(${{field-3}}$,\,\infty )$

feedback.worked_solution:
To solve this inequality using the graphical method, we first need to move all of the numbers to the left-hand side so that the right-hand side is $0.$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5{x}^{2} & >10x \\ -5{x}^{2}-10x & >0.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we want to find the values of $x$ for which the parabola $y=-5{x}^{2}-10x$ lies above the $x$-axis. Let's find the roots of the parabola by factoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5{x}^{2}-10x & =0 \\ -5x(x+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

We see that the roots are $x=0$ and $x=-2,$ and we can graph the parabola as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14004892/assets/6cb044d4c6280d77dd525f6e2a8702d9fcba1553c2d33411407d69e09a6b715b.png)

Since we are interested in solving 

$$
-5{x}^{2}-10x>0,
$$

we look for the part of the parabola that is above the $x$-axis. 

Based on the graph, the solution is $-2<x<0.$ 

Using interval notation, we write $x\in (-2,0).$
